quotes.text: And, just to add, this doesn’t mean folks should be compensated any less. With AI rapidly progressing, and potential quantum computing breakthroughs, the reality is less and less jobs will be needed. But the needs for housing, food, and healthcare will be the same. We need UBI. https://t.co/EDeemm60RY

AI is projected to replace 30% of US jobs in just 5 years. We have to let go of this archaic belief that we need to earn our basic needs through labor. Soon enough, there won’t be anymore labor to give. 

That’s why I’m running for Congress, to codify our right to basic needs. That includes housing, healthcare, public education, and nutritional food.

AI has only developed this rapidly because of our tax dollars and by learning from centuries of our ingenuity. What good is this technology if it doesn’t deliver on the future we were promised where we work less and live more?

And yet, it’s the super rich donors who are steering our parties and our government! We need to clean house and get their influence out of our politics.

There’s too much at stake with wealth inequality, AI, and the climate crisis threatening our futures. Enough is enough. https://t.co/zCJDk7cPZj

What happens when we lose millions of jobs to automation over the next decade? People are already finding it impossible to find jobs today!

What the hell is the point of AI if it’s not making our lives easier?

We need to guarantee every American’s right to our basic needs ASAP. https://t.co/OMzOU82cpE

Never mind most companies still aren’t seeing a return on AI, but when they replace every job with automation, who’s going to be left to buy anything?

This short-sighted, profit-at-all-costs mentality is going to crash our economy.

We need to regulate AI and put workers first. https://t.co/fIuQksrDy3

Do you want these same people in charge of how we develop AI?

We need to regulate Big Tech, ASAP. https://t.co/mQBDfCkGki

Well, this is just silly. By this logic, the public should have had no say in banning asbestos or lead-based paint. The regulatory body that should decide these questions should of course have intimate knowledge of AI, but so should ordinary folks who will be the most impacted by its development. Ironically, the foremost experts of AI are begging for some form of regulations because they understand the dangers of this technology better than anyone. You also never answered my question. I suggest you stop letting boogeywords like “socialism” stop you from critically thinking about our greatest challenges. This isn’t a zero-sum game. We can protect American jobs while protecting the ability to innovate.

Should we allow AI to continue to develop unregulated then? I have no interest in stopping innovation, but why shouldn’t the publi have a say over how it’s developed when it’s our ingenuity that’s made it successful in the first place? With tens of millions of jobs and our already fragile energy grids, what else should we do? I’m sincerely asking.

This is the right thing to do.

AI has the potential to help solve some of our greatest problems, but only if we democratize how it’s developed.

Leaving it in the hands of tech oligarchs will destroy our energy grids and wipe out countless jobs just to fill our feeds with slop. https://t.co/LS8C0ZvHUY

I don’t think that’s necessarily true. The housing crisis is also an issue of over regulation, monopoly developers, and private equity firms preventing the large scale building of affordable homes. For healthcare, I’m calling for Medicare for all, guaranteeing universal coverage. UBI will be necessary to protecting the working class in the new age of AI, but I don’t think we’re there just yet.

@NewProgressUSA I absolutely think we’ll need UBI in the future, especially as AI develops and continues to change our culture of “work,” as we know it. But right now, I’m focused on addressing the health care and housing crisis first.

The law has already sorted out contributory negligence, I’m not basing that out with you, except to say that some of the victims were kids. Surely you can agree that we should regulate AI chatbots to protect deeply impressionable children from danger? I agree that most politician are bought and paid for. I’m not taking a dime in corporate/lobby money for that reason. I don’t think this very productive for either of us but I’ll just say this again. This isn’t a zero-sum game, we can have innovation and protect working people too, but only if work worth together in good faith to do so.

It’s not just about protecting jobs. It’s about making sure people will still have their basic needs met when AI completely changes the culture of “work” in our society. I’m excited about the prospect of how AI will improve our daily lives, but it’s developing so rapidly that we’re not thinking clearly about the dangers it risks too. If we don’t, we risk doing far more damage with this technology than good.

AI chatbots have convinced several people to commit suicide in just the last 2 years. AI is capable of creating photos and videos that are indistinguishable from reality. AI data centers are developing so quickly that they’re draining our energy grids. We absolutely need regulations on this technology and we need it ASAP.

5.3M views on an AI generated video Elon Musk reposted that’s designed to manufacture consent for a regime change war for oil that NO ONE wants while housing and healthcare costs continue to skyrocket here at home.

Wtf are we doing here? https://t.co/EuWyALP4pi

We need leaders who won’t be corrupted by the billionaires who want to use AI to just enrich themselves. 

AI has the potential to save our most pressing problems, but only if we hold those developing it accountable. That’s why I’m running for Congress. https://t.co/Q1MwvGgb0w

Putting the ad for a $20 AI sub in this article aside…there’s still cause for concern here.

We need to be prepared for how everyday workers will be impacted by AI.

That means fighting for stronger labor laws, raising min wage, and a federal guarantee of our most basic needs. https://t.co/euHiiEuBS1

My number one priority in Congress will be to get big money the hell out of our politics.

We can’t get Medicare for All, universal childcare, or AI regulations until we root out this blatant corruption once and for all.

It’s time for publicly financed elections. https://t.co/WTPV2gkbCf

This is how disposable we are to the billionaires developing AI.

That’s why I’m calling for regulations on AI and the data centers that are straining our energy grids.

There’s too much at stake with this technology, and we need to make sure AI benefits us all, not just the few. https://t.co/jsQ3oQN1hA

If you’re in NC-04, vote for @NidaAllam!

If you’re not, donate! AIPAC & AI are pouring millions into the race and every donation will make a difference.

We’re not waiting till we win to build a coalition, that work starts now, and I’m honored to be fighting alongside Nida. https://t.co/2gXzjy1Yoc

This is the EXACT kind of leadership we need in this moment.

Bernie and AOC are reclaiming our leverage over these AI companies and forcing them to contribute to the solutions we desperately need to protect jobs, bring down energy costs, and end mass surveillance. https://t.co/MxftR2GFUk

Bernie & AOC are leading the way on this. We need a data center moratorium to force companies to the table to address the greatest problems this tech brings.

AI isn’t going anywhere, but neither are we, and we need real protections for our jobs, our environment, and our privacy. https://t.co/hqNWBbWLrL

For folks who think this is an exaggeration, AI has already figured out how to lie, to resist being shut down, and to escape testing grounds.

If AI achieves super intelligence w/o guardrails in place, we’ll be as significant to them as ants are to us.

We are not alarmed enough. https://t.co/ctuLLpYWv0

This is our leverage as government. We take that leverage with these data center moratoriums and we force (tech companies) to the table, so they can agree to regulations that will protect our resources, protect our safety and our security, and ensure that we are not completely destroying our labor economy as well.

This is the way. 

Human ingenuity is what fuels AI. The public deserves to reap the benefits. 

I would sign up to co-sponsor this bill on Day 1. https://t.co/EcSdEQEtco

They formed a super PAC overnight to spend $350K against us. 

Whether it’s AIPAC, AI, or big pharma, they’re used to buying and owning this seat, and now they’re hiding from the voters to do it.

Denver is about to remind them that this seat belongs to us. https://t.co/aXcIXyMvRu

All of these celebrities and politicians suddenly parroting all the same pro-AI lines is not a coincidence.

The industry knows how unpopular they are with the people so they’re spending millions to mislead us and keep candidates who will fight to regulate them out of office. https://t.co/9lTc8aAOFU

I think it’s also something that has motivated me into making sure that we sign on finally onto the UN’s Declaration of Human Rights and guaranteeing the rights to housing and health care and nutritional food as basic rights in our Constitution. Because if, you know, AI changes work as we know it, and the social contract that we have is that if you work, then that contract is broken and you need to replace it with something else that protects people’s dignity. And so this is going to change everything, and I don’t think we have enough folks that are talking about it in a meaningful way.
We’re talking about fascism. We’re talking about climate apocalypse. We’re talking about a complete and dramatic upheaval of the labor economy because of job automation and the advancement of AI.

I do feel like there is an interesting connection that I think is being intentionally and correctly drawn between AI and our climate right now in a way that is going to propel us toward being able to pass some really meaningful climate legislation.
the missing component of AI, and how that all factors into all of our legislation, specifically when it comes to the climate, that we need to be focused on.

We are not angry enough about AI.

We need to regulate this industry. Now. https://t.co/NDb1I3UMtf

Bernie’s right. Republican mega-donors are pouring tens of millions of dollars into our primaries through AI, AIPAC, and crypto’s super PACs.

Enough is enough. 

We need to ban super PACs from our primaries, end Citizens United, and pass publicly financed elections. https://t.co/ot3h9KaLi0

We need to pause the development of ASI and pass aggressive AI regulations now. 

Whether it’s the threat of a technology we can’t control, the massive market bubble from these companies, or the catastrophic impacts on our environment & global workforce, we cannot afford to wait. https://t.co/R05fJJbbTy

We need to regulate AI for all of the existential threats it poses to our climate, economy, and democracy, but we cannot expect the very people who got us into this mess to self-regulate their way out.

Congress needs to act now and guard against ANY corporate influence. https://t.co/c9VFixGmiy

Denver voters have made clear that they are very concerned about AI data centers straining our grid and spiking electric bills while a few corporations profit. I support Senator Sanders and Representative Ocasio-Cortez’s data center moratorium — not to stop innovation, but to force these corporations to the table and ensure they are accountable.

That’s the kind of foreign policy that’s actually in line with the values of the American people and would actually lead to true peace building and true cooperation on the global stage, that we are desperately in need of, especially in this moment as we’re facing the crises of things like AI and climate change.
